title: DNA and Genetics Basics
text: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is the molecule that carries genetic instructions for the development, functioning, and reproduction of living organisms. It consists of two strands forming a double helix, made of four nucleotide bases (adenine, thymine, guanine, cytosine). Genes are segments of DNA that code for proteins. Genetic information is passed from parents to offspring, and variations (mutations) in DNA are a source of biological diversity and, occasionally, disease.
